name: Tarneeb
description: Tarneeb (Arabic for 'Trump') is a popular trick-taking card game in the Middle East (Levant, Egypt). It is a partnership game for 4 players. Teams bid on how many tricks they can take (starting from 7 up to 13). The highest bidder names the trump suit (Tarneeb). The objective is to fulfill the bid.

history.origins: Roots in the Middle East; likely influenced by Whist and Bridge. The name comes from the Arabic word for trump.
timeline: 20th century: Widely played across the Levant and Egypt; Egyptian variant with trump-suit bidding documented.
history.cultural: Extremely popular social game in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Palestine, and Egypt.
history.evolution: Various regional scoring limits (31, 41, 61) and bidding styles (Egyptian vs Syrian).

rules.objective: Win at least as many tricks as bid. First team to reach target score (e.g., 31, 41, or 61) wins.
rules.gameplay: Bidding starts at 7 tricks. Players bid number of tricks (7-13) or pass. Highest bidder declares Trump (Tarneeb). Player to dealer's right (or bidder) leads first. Must follow suit. Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit. Winner leads next.

strategy.basic: Bid on long suits (5+ cards) with high honors (A, K). Count trumps played. Support partner if they bid.
strategy.intermediate: Lead trumps early to clear opponents' trumps if you are declarer. If defending, try to force declarer to ruff (use trumps) when they are weak.
strategy.advanced: Signal partner with discards (high/low). Calculate 'losing tricks' to estimate bid. Squeeze opponents in end-game.
tips: A bid of 7 usually requires a 5-card suit and some aces.
Kaboot (13 tricks) is rare and risky but high reward.

scoring.description: If declaring team wins bid details: Score = Tricks taken. Bonus often applies for 13 (Kaboot). If they fail: Score = Negative of bid (or zero for opponents, or opponents score tricks taken + bonus). Non-bidding team scores tricks taken (unless bidder fails). Exact scoring varies by region (e.g. Tarneeb 41 rules).
